rationale.conceptual: Standard application of DFT to compute total energies of magnetic phases of Fe using an existing all-electron code. No novel method or algorithm, just a known physical system and standard magnetic orderings.
rationale.execution: Requires orchestrating an external DFT code with a geometry optimization (c parameter scan) for three magnetic configurations. Though steps are sequential, setting up the tool, ensuring convergence, and handling file I/O adds moderate engineering effort.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires standard DFT calculations for a simple 4-atom system using an existing all-electron code. The method is well-established, and the pipeline is short, though it involves geometry optimization. Resources are minimal, no GPU needed.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small 4-atom unit cell FLAPW calculation, run on CPU with minimal memory; no large datasets.
